chunks: Do you think that giving a drink of water to the pilgrims and going on a visit to the Sacred Mosque, is the same as believing in God and the Last Day, and striving in the cause of God? In the eyes of God it is not the same; and God does not show the unrighteous the way.

key_terms.جَاهَدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: striving in the cause of God

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the deeds of the polytheists and the Prophet Muhammad according to Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah At-Tawbah (9:17) establishes a fundamental Shia theological principle that ritual service (khidmah) to the Sacred Mosque, performed by the Quraysh, holds no merit without accompanying true faith (iman) and striving (jihād). It contrasts the superficial piety of the polytheists with the comprehensive devotion of the Prophet, emphasizing that God does not guide those who are unjust (ẓālimīn) in their core beliefs. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of action and belief, where deeds are validated by their spiritual foundation.
